a:r.a:t: GPCRs Function in Vision and Olfaction

p:cNvPr.descr: This diagram represents the molecular consequences of photon absorption by rhodopsin in the rod outer segment. Pictured is a tan rectangular box outlined, representing the plasma membrane, and in it is another rectangular box that is shaded horizontally in two brown tones. The top section of the inner rectangle, labeled “Excitation,” is a light tan color. The bottom part, labeled “Recovery/Adaptation,” is a darker tan color. In the first stage, light absorption, which is represented by a yellowish-orange squiggly arrow, converts 11-cisretinal to all-transretinal, activating rhodopsin (Rh), which is a pinkish structure. In the second stage, activated rhodopsin catalyzes replacement of GDP by GTP on transducin (T), which then dissociates into T alpha-GTP and T beta gamma. T beta gamma and T alpha-GDP are represented by two green structures; once GTP is introduced into the reaction and GDP leaves, an arrow indicates the production of T alpha-GTP, which is also represented by a green structure with hairlike projections all around it. Next to it is a blue structure that represents phosphodiesterase (PDE). In the third stage, Ta-GTP activates cGMP phosphodiesterase (PDE) by binding and removing its inhibitory subunit (I), represented by a gray circle with an “I” on it. An arrow points to the T alpha-GTP structure with the I attached to it, along with the PDE, now with hairlike extensions around it – this represents active PDE. An arrow, which represents cGMP, pointing upward moves through the PDE, forming 5’-GMP. This is stage 4 of the process, where active PDE reduces [cGMP] to below the level needed to keep cation channels open. In stage 5, cation channels, represented by purple structures on the outline of the large rectangle, close, preventing influx of Na+ and Ca2+. In stage 6, the continued efflux of Ca2+ through the Na+-Ca2+ exchanger, represented by a gray oval, reduces cytosolic [Ca2+]. In stage 7, the reduction of [Ca2+] activates guanylyl cyclase (GC), which is represented by light blue ovals with hairlike extensions around it, and inhibits PDE; [cGMP] rises toward “dark” level, reopening cation channels and returning Vm to pre-stimulus level. To the left, Ca2+ stimulates a reaction between Rhodopsin kinase (RK) and rhodopsin. RK is represented by a light blur rectangle with three Ps in red circles in them; the Ps represent the phosphorylation of rhodopsin. To the left, Arrestin (Arr) binds phosphorylated carboxyl terminus, inactivating rhodopsin. Arrestin is represented by an orangish square box with three Ps bound vertically to Rhodopsin. A dashed arrow points to another Rh to the left. In the last stage, arrestin dissociates, 8 rhodopsin is dephosphorylated, and all-transretinal is replaced with 11-cis-retinal. Rhodopsin is ready for another phototransduction cycle after this.
